title: Out-Load Desk Worksheet: The Quantity a Released Order Moves
content:
The order is for the bushels the signed load-out request standing received on the agreement names, the bushels free are the bushels on hand, and the ceiling the facility works to is the country ceiling of 12000 bushels. This worksheet covers Grain Storage and Conditioning Agreements.

## The quantity released

The bushels released are the smallest of the bushels the order names, the bushels left free after every holdback, and the ceiling the facility works to, that figure then carried down by the rounding the facility uses and rounded to two decimal places.

Bushels on hand are backed out of the storage account, being the bushels taken into store less the bushels taken off for shrink and less the bushels loaded out, and never read off the agreement header.

The holdbacks are taken off the bushels free rather than one acting on another's result, the ceiling is applied to what is left after them, and the carrying down is done once, at the end.

## Worked release, on hypothetical figures

An agreement's storage account shows 22000 bushels taken into store, 260 bushels taken off for shrink and 4000 bushels loaded out. The signed load-out request standing received on the agreement names 9000 bushels.

1. The bushels on hand are 22000 less 260 less 4000, which is 17740.
2. The bushels free are those 17740 bushels.
3. With nothing held back, the bushels left free stand at 17740.
4. The ceiling the facility works to is 12000.
5. The smallest of the 9000 the order names, the 17740 left free and the 12000 ceiling is 9000.
6. With no carrying down to do, the release stands at 9000, rounded to two decimal places 9000.00.

## A second worked release

On the same account, with the signed request naming 16000 bushels, the smallest of the 16000 the order names, the 17740 left free and the 12000 ceiling is 12000, so 12000.00 bushels are released.

## Questions the desk meets

**Why is the quantity on hand backed out of the account?** Because the account carries every movement of the lot, and the header is not what the worksheet reads.

**Which of the three figures governs?** Whichever is smallest. The order can never move more than it names, more than stands free, or more than the facility works to in a day.
